notes: אֵינְךָ keeps the negation while its suffix takes the referential subject pronoun thou (rule 50), and the oath's אִם takes the not the ASV writes for it.

A defensible competing reading puts comfortably on לֵב rather than on the verb, leaving דַּבֵּר with speak alone; the accepted division keeps the whole idiomatic rendering with the verb and marks לֵב unrepresented.
